source_ref: Held 2025, 20; Udovitch 1962, 198; van Doosselaere 2009, 65; Harris 2020 (SSRN draft), pp. 25-27, 31
notes: NOT BLIND (README leak 1; priors B5). The contract names who bears the peril: Held 20 quotes 'dicti solidi sunt ad periculum dicti [name of the commendator] maris et gentis clarefactum', a formula 'common in Venetian documents of the time'; Udovitch 198: loss 'borne exclusively by the investor(s)'. No premium is paid to an outsider (not spreading), and no member's loss is mutualised (commenda LR4). Harris 2020, 31 names the triad but does not place the commenda in it.

source_ref: Harris 2007 (conf. draft), PDF p. 34; van Doosselaere 2009, 102-104
notes: Harris PDF 34: 'The commenda was a voluntary contractual institution'. vD 102-104: partners were chosen opportunistically, venture by venture.

source_ref: González de Lara 2002, 259; Held 2025, 20; Udovitch 1962, 198; Harris 2007 (conf. draft), PDF p. 10
notes: González de Lara 259 (Venice): merchants 'were partially insured against the risk of sea and people, for they were exempted from repayment beyond the amount saved from loss at sea or through the abuse of property rights abroad, if this was clearly apparent'. Held 20 quotes the formula '... ad periculum dicti [commendator] maris et gentis clarefactum', 'common in Venetian documents'. Udovitch 198: 'borne exclusively by the investor(s), the agent losing only his expended time and effort'. Articulated on the quoted formula. Medium: Udovitch 198 ('profits and risks are shared by both parties') and Harris 2020, 26 ('the risks are split') count the agent's labour and expected share as at risk, which would read 'shared'. Held's Venetian claim rests on González de Lara 2008 (n.53), so Held and González de Lara are partly one witness here.

source_ref: Udovitch 1962, 198; Harris 2007 (conf. draft), PDF p. 10; van Doosselaere 2009, 129
notes: Udovitch 198: no agent liability for loss 'from an unsuccessful business venture'; Harris PDF 10: 'travel-related loss or trade-related loss'; vD 129: 'An unprofitable commenda was a legal, albeit not desirable, business outcome leaving little recourse for the investor.' Medium for the same labour caveat as RB1.

source_ref: van Doosselaere 2009, 64-78, 138; Held 2025, 12 n. 26
notes: No work states any security for the commenda capital. vD 138 on collateral concerns loans only; Held 12 n.26 describes Ragusan enforcement against an absent debtor, not a pledge. The priors' 'none' was general knowledge.

source_ref: Harris 2007 (conf. draft), PDF p. 10; van Doosselaere 2009, 129; Udovitch 1962, 198; González de Lara 2002, 259
notes: Harris PDF 10: the traveller 'did not have to return that part of the capital that was lost, even when it was the entire sum invested'; vD 129; Udovitch 198 ('partial or total loss'). González de Lara 259 makes the exemption conditional on the loss being 'clearly apparent'. Exception on fault or breach: vD 74; Harris PDF 10.

source_ref: van Doosselaere 2009, 66-67, 130; Held 2025, 11 n. 20; Harris 2020 (SSRN draft), pp. 26-27
notes: vD 66-67: the payout 'followed a fixed rule and was virtually independent of either the business characteristics at hand or the social circumstances of the partners'; only 'a handful' of 4,860 ties (1154-1265) depart from one-fourth/three-fourths. Contrast sea-loan rates varying by destination (vD 130). Held 11 n.20: in Venice the tractator's quarter was 'vastly prevailing' in the first half of the 13th century. The investor carries the peril against a customary share; no price is set on the peril. Dissent: Harris 2020, 26 argues that the shares 'could be viewed as a mode of pricing the risks', then leaves the question under-determined (27); by the PR1 rule that reading is analyst-imposed.

source_ref: González de Lara 2002, 258-260; Held 2025, 21 and n. 54; Harris 2020 (SSRN draft), pp. 26-27
notes: González de Lara 258-259 (Venice): the state 'developed various institutional arrangements that generated and transmitted the verifiable information required to adjudicate commercial disputes'; 'State delegates in the Venetian colonies abroad, scribes en route, and public mediators in Venice carefully monitored commercial ventures'. The exemption held 'if this was clearly apparent' (259). Held 21: 'clarefactum refers to the need that the occurrence of such extraordinary events ... had to be sufficiently clarified'; n.54 cites a 1253 Ragusan court proceeding on a travelling merchant's culpability, hedged 'it is possible'. Low: González de Lara 2002 is a dissertation summary stating a mechanism, not a case. Alternative 'documentary' (Harris 2020, 26-27: itinerary, bills of lading and accounts, checked by the investor). [2026-10-12, later: adjudication replaced -> overruled by ruling 26, which recoded the cell claimant-oath (LM-R0066).]

source_ref: González de Lara 2002, 259; Held 2025, 13, 20-21; Harris 2007 (conf. draft), PDF p. 10; van Doosselaere 2009, 74

For the Italian contract the fault limb rests on Harris and vD; the verbatim fault clause is Ragusan.

source_ref: Ackerman-Lieberman 2011, JESHO 54, 662 (the active partner as paid bailee, after Maimonides); Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:8 and Shevu'ot 7:8 (Sefaria, Koren-Steinsaltz English); Exodus 22:9-10; Udovitch 1970, Studia Islamica 32, 292 (JTS ENA 4011, f. 57a); Ackerman-Lieberman 2012, 1033
notes: claimant-oath (third instance; value added 2026-10-11, records/RULINGS-comanda-adjudications-2026-10-11.md, ruling 2), LOW AND ANALYST-IMPOSED because the chain is the analyst's: no source applies the bailee's oath to the 'isqa in terms. (i) On the pikkadon half the manager is a PAID bailee (Ackerman-Lieberman 2011, 662). (ii) A paid bailee swears for an animal injured, captured or dead beyond his control and is exempt; he pays for loss and theft (Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:8; Exodus 22:9-10, the owner 'shall accept it'). So unavoidable peril on that half is established by his oath - DECISIVE in the normative text, unless witnesses show fault. (iii) Practice: partners, sharecroppers and stewards swear even without a definite claim (Mishnah Shevu'ot 7:8); a Fustat court in 1125 had a partner demand 'a Partner's Oath' over lost capital (Udovitch 1970, 292); Rabbanite court decisions 'often demanded that one or more parties take an oath' (Ackerman-Lieberman 2012, 1033). On the milveh half nothing is verified: the debt survives the loss. Previously .NR.

LS3=1 for a kō needs either the association route (a member answers for others' obligations) or the debtor route (the drawer expressly liable beyond the pledge with his person or whole estate; sea_loan, bodemerij_amsterdam). The clause relied on, 質物書入 under 手形 with the town officers' 裏印, secures the winner's own agreed repayment; it neither binds his person or whole estate nor makes any member answer for another. A pledge alone is .NR on the general question, not 0 (bodemerij_amsterdam note); 0 would need liability confined to the pledge (bottomry). The old note's observation stands as description: the security attaches on winning, not on membership. source_read none: recoded from the clause as quoted, 加藤 1998 not reopened.
